lc_person: Geoffrey Russell Searle, emeritus professor of British history at the University of East Anglia; author of The Quest for National Efficiency (1971).
item_person: G. R. Searle (Geoffrey Russell Searle), historian and professor, sharing LC n87804313, GND 130169803 and VIAF 4146522428132392411 with the LC authority.

evidence.says: The authority expands G. R. to Geoffrey Russell, cites The Quest for National Efficiency (1971), and identifies the author of Miles Edmund Cotman (2014) as a UEA emeritus professor of British history. It links Q5512413, GND 130169803 and VIAF 4146522428132392411. Its birthDate is 1921, supported by a Wikipedia note viewed in September 2014.

English label G. R. Searle, alias Geoffrey Russell Searle, description historian and professor; P244 is n87804313, P227 is 130169803 and P214 is 4146522428132392411. P569 gives 1940, citing Libris authority 235901.

The Swedish national library catalogue authority gives G. R. Searle (Geoffrey Russell), 1940-, describes him as emeritus professor of history at UEA, and connects The Quest for National Efficiency (1971), Corruption in British Politics (1987) and A New England? (2004). This directly supports 1940 for the same author.

The exact Open Library author in key_evidence has The Quest for National Efficiency, Corruption in British Politics, Eugenics and Politics in Britain, Morality and the Market in Victorian Britain and A New England?, matching the LC person and institutional bibliography.

Geoffrey Searle is professor emeritus of history at UEA; publications include The Quest for National Efficiency (1971), Corruption in British Politics (1987) and Morality and the Market in Victorian Britain (1998). No birth year is supplied.
UEA identifies Geoffrey Searle as emeritus professor in its School of History and Art History and lists A New England? Peace and War 1886-1918 (2004).
The search-indexed article gives 1941 and identifies the same UEA historian and works; this differs from both LC and Libris and is only a secondary lead.

notes: The birth disagreement does not indicate two people: names, works, affiliation and shared identifiers agree. Prefer 1940 provisionally on the directly checked Libris authority; LC 1921 derives from an older Wikipedia citation, while the search-indexed Wikipedia article gives 1941. No institutional biography or CV confirming the exact birth year was found.
